title: inquiries/1
description: What people wrote to the client asking about its products, as written, with where they wrote from. Whoever receives an inquiry writes it; sdr reads it, keeps each one as received, and records the person's own message as the evidence that they asked to be answered.
x-producer: any operator that receives an inquiry (seo for site forms, gads and meta-ads for lead ads)
x-rules: An inquiry is what a person wrote to the client, kept as written: the words are never summarised, translated or tidied.
An inquiry_id is stable: the same message has the same id in every document, so the reader never records it twice.
The producer sends what the person gave and nothing it looked up: no enrichment, no guessed company, no inferred country.

The reader keeps each inquiry as received before it uses it. A message that came from the person's own mailbox (channel email) or from a form whose address they confirmed (email_confirmed true) is the evidence of their consent to be answered at that address, and only that; a form nobody confirmed proves nothing about the address typed into it.
An absent optional key means unknown, never null and never an empty string.

producer.description: The pack that wrote the document (its CLI word).

produced_at.description: When the document was written: ISO 8601 with its zone.

inquiries.description: The inquiries; empty when none came.

inquiry_id.description: Unique and stable for the message.

received_at.description: When the client received it: ISO 8601 with its zone.

language.description: The language they wrote in, an ISO 639-1 code, when the producer knows it.

company.description: The company they named, as they named it.

domain.description: Its website's domain, without a scheme.

country.description: Its country, an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code, when they gave it.

page_url.description: The page they wrote from, when there is one.

campaign.description: The campaign or tag the visit came from, as the producer recorded it.

agreement_text.description: The words of the consent box they ticked, when the form had one.

email_confirmed.description: True when the person proved the address is theirs (they followed a link sent to it, or wrote from it); absent means nobody checked.
